questions.why: Use 'Do' for yes/no questions with 'you' in the present simple.
Use 'Does' with third person singular (he/she/it) in present simple questions.
Use 'Did' for all subjects in past simple yes/no questions.
Past simple wh-questions use 'did' + base verb.
'The film' is third person singular, so use 'does' in the present simple.
In present continuous questions the auxiliary 'are' comes before the subject.
'What' asks about things or meanings.
'When' asks about time.

questions.q: ___ many people came to the party?
questions.why: 'How many' asks about quantity with countable nouns.
When 'who' is the subject, use no auxiliary: 'Who broke...?'

questions.q: Object question: Who ___ you invite to dinner?
questions.why: When 'who' is the object, use the auxiliary 'did' + base verb.

questions.q: Which sentence is a subject question?
questions.why: A subject question has no auxiliary; the verb agrees directly with 'who'.
Subject 'who' takes a singular verb and no auxiliary: 'Who wants...?'
'What' is the subject here, so use no auxiliary: 'What happened?'
A positive statement takes a negative tag using the same auxiliary.
A negative statement takes a positive tag with the matching auxiliary.
Past simple statements use 'didn't' in the question tag.
After 'Let's', the question tag is 'shall we'.
The tag for 'I am' is the irregular 'aren't I'.

questions.q: Indirect: Could you tell me where ___?
questions.why: Indirect questions use statement word order, not inversion.

questions.q: Indirect: Do you know what time ___?
questions.why: After 'Do you know...' use statement order with no 'does'.

questions.q: Indirect: I wonder ___ she has arrived.
questions.why: Indirect yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether'.

options: Can you tell me where is the toilet?
Can you tell me where the toilet is?
Can you tell me where does the toilet?
Can you tell me where the toilet?
questions.answer: Can you tell me where the toilet is?
questions.why: Indirect questions keep subject-verb order with no auxiliary inversion.
In everyday English 'Who...for?' is normal, keeping the preposition at the end.
'Look for' means to search; the preposition 'for' goes to the end of the question.
'Come from' shows origin; the preposition stays at the end of the question.

questions.q: Who did you talk ___ at the meeting?
questions.why: 'Talk to' takes 'to', which goes to the end of the question.

questions.q: Type the auxiliary: '___ he play tennis on Sundays?'
questions.why: Third person singular present simple questions use 'does'.

questions.q: Type the question tag: 'You can drive, ___?'
questions.why: A positive statement with 'can' takes the negative tag 'can't you'.

questions.q: Subject or object? Type one word for the gap: 'Who ___ you meet yesterday?'
questions.why: This is an object question, so it needs the auxiliary 'did'.
